title: Becoming Hamlet at Five Angels Theater #becominghamlet #audienceparti...
transcript: My friend described this show as “drama therapy core,” which feels apt given its workshoppy and participatory nature. It's basically a one-act version of Hamlet where the audience collectively assumes the titular role. The level of participation varies — some of it is just through call and response, some folks have pre-assigned lines, and some audience members actually go on stage to participate in the given scene. It's well-organized with facilitators constantly moving around the theatre to help prompt and physically direct people when necessary. It's a cool concept, but dependent on whether or not you have an audience that's game. As a production of Hamlet, it's not quite as successful. I found that the participatory nature of the show overshadowed the story, and a lot of my attention was spent just following the action in the room. It's kind of overwhelming from an auditory processing perspective, with lines constantly coming from different people all over the theatre. It was an undoubtedly engaging experience, but if I didn't already know the story of Hamlet, I don't think I'd know it now. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer praises the concept and engagement but criticizes it as a production of Hamlet, saying the participatory nature overshadowed the story. Clear mixed verdict with pros and cons balanced.
